# 2023-604 — Quixilver: 2023 published robot (name not independently confirmed)

Primary source: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-presents-our-2023-robot-and-code-release/447255

Reviewed 2026-10-26. This is a source-bounded technical study. Construction, stated intent, interpretation and unresolved evidence are separate.

## 2023 published robot account · intake

### Published construction or code

A pasta-roller intake grips a cone flange and pinches a cube, constraining cones to tip-in or tip-out. A roller reorienter supplies the additional rotational degree of freedom needed for an upright handoff. Rollers are powered coaxially through the reorienter.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team wanted ground pickup in arbitrary orientations; human-player throwing could shorten travel by an estimated 40% and reduce loading-zone traffic. Coaxial drive protects motors and reduces mass at the intake edge.

### Engineering interpretation

This is an explicit strategy-to-mechanism chain: changing the pickup source reduces travel only if orientation and handoff remain reliable. The 40% is the team’s route estimate, not an independently measured cycle improvement. A broad capture envelope transfers complexity downstream unless the robot can reduce the resulting pose uncertainty. Compare full acquisition-to-scoring cycles, including difficult orientations, rather than pickup speed alone.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## 2023 published robot account · transfer

### Published construction or code

A linear intake slider brings the piece inward and permits frontal compliance. A separate horizontal scoring-arm slider reaches across the intake. A time-of-flight sensor first distinguishes orientation at a fixed location, then locates the piece laterally. The elevator lowers while the intake expels to hand off.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team needed handoff despite variable piece position across the intake width.

### Engineering interpretation

Do not collapse the two sliders into a single motion. The intake reduces some uncertainty, then sensing and the receiving mechanism handle what remains. This avoids requiring perfect passive centering, at the cost of coordinated motion, sensor interpretation and collision clearance. Sensor occlusion, flange shape, cone reflectivity and loaded mechanism deflection are plausible validation concerns, not failures established by this publication.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## 2023 published robot account · scoring

### Published construction or code

A non-parallel four-bar provides scoring reach. An Everybot-style lightweight gripper squeezes the cone tip and pinches a cube. The release describes scoring all levels.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team chose the linkage for low mass and long extension, and judged the high-versus-middle scoring difference sufficient to justify the added capability.

### Engineering interpretation

The linkage choice belongs with the piece acquisition and handoff design. Saving moving mass can reduce the drive and tipping burden, but linkage workspace, joint play and gripper compliance determine the usable placement envelope. A later team using a single-stage elevator should not be read as proof that this four-bar was a failed architecture; the game, interface and required motion differ.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## 2023 published robot account · controls

### Published construction or code

Originally the operator selected scoring locations on a driverstation keyboard and the driver triggered automated scoring. The team later reports the driver becoming faster and more consistent than that sequence, reducing the operator role to piece and level selection.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The control allocation evolved with driver performance.

### Engineering interpretation

Automation should be judged against practiced human operation, including recovery, rather than valued simply because it exists. This is a useful counterexample to treating 604’s later single-driver automation as an unchanging philosophy implemented identically every year. Keep the final software release and its 2024-beta port distinct. Detailed drivetrain specifications and the charge-station balancing mechanism are not established by this reviewed release.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Evidence limits

- Selected primary publications/code reviewed; exact per-event installation and exhaustive intermediate revisions remain unresolved.
- Four previously blocked source originals (2023 robot photo; 2026 serializer, intake and hopper CAD views) were recovered through normal browser downloads on 2026-10-26 and inspected. Whole-robot source views are not exhaustive mechanism or event-version certification.

The reviewed publication does not establish charge-station balance construction or exact drivetrain hardware. FIRST’s carried-forward robot-name field is not treated as authoritative identity for this different-season machine.

source_reviews.title: Quixilver 2023 Robot and Code Release
source_reviews.locator: Post 1, Strategic Design, Intake, Handoff and Scoring Arm, Code Release
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the team's written retrospective through the web tool.
source_reviews.facts: Documents the orientation and translation stages, range-based transfer, scoring linkage and operator role change.
source_reviews.limitations: Cycle-distance savings are the team's estimate. The post warns that CAD is mirrored from the physical robot.

source_reviews.title: Quixilver FRC-2023 code
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the three command implementations in the released 2023 tree.
source_reviews.facts: The measure pose depends on orientation. The transverse axis clamps and updates its target from filtered range. Handoff commands release, receive, lift and clearance movements.
source_reviews.limitations: The release also contains a separate beta migration. Code review here uses FRC-2023 and does not establish which build ran at each event.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Quixilver designed its cycle around acquiring ground cones from arbitrary approaches, reducing the need to queue for the double substation. Its floor intake captures first and resolves orientation later. Two translation tasks are distinct: the intake slider pulls the captured piece toward the center of the chassis, and the scoring assembly moves across the roller width to meet its actual lateral location. The four-bar and elevator carry the received piece to the grid. Quixilver believed a single extra cycle could matter in a close match and reported an estimated 40 percent reduction in trip distance for the single-substation route they analyzed.
source_review.piece_flow: Opposed intake rollers grab a cone flange or pinch a cube. Cone capture collapses many floor angles into two cases, tip in or tip out. The software uses a distance comparison at a prescribed geometry to choose the orientation case. The roller assembly rotates the piece upright for the exchange, and the intake slider brings the piece inward. Another filtered distance reading determines the cross-chassis handoff position. At the meeting point the elevator lowers the receiving gripper, the intake rollers expel and the gripper receives. The handoff command also lifts toward a post-transfer height, pulls the arm toward its minimum angle and commands the appropriate slider clearance. The same gripper pinches cubes or grips cones near the tip and rides the scoring assembly to the chosen level.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: Roller drive crosses the reorienter pivot coaxially so the motors can be placed away from the vulnerable outside edge. Intake fore-aft slider motion creates a capture-to-transfer stroke and provides some compliance in head-on contact. Cross-chassis motion solves a separate offset along the rollers. The code clips its lateral target to the axis limits and revises it if filtered piece position moves enough during alignment. Inference: the achievable handoff region is the intersection of the two axes' travel, sensor view, intake release geometry and gripper compliance.

subsystems.name: Floor intake and reorienter
subsystems.construction: Pasta-style paired rollers, powered rotating roller assembly and linear intake slider. Roller power passes through the reorienter coaxially.
subsystems.operation: The rollers grip the piece and constrain cone direction to one of two states. The rotating assembly makes a pose suitable for transfer.
subsystems.team_rationale: Quixilver sought ground acquisition regardless of cone orientation, with the motor mass and exposure reduced at the intake's leading edge.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The two-state assumption is valuable only if skewed cones settle into one of those states with predictable range readings.
subsystems.interfaces: Coaxial transmission crosses a moving pivot. Slider alignment fixes the receiver's fore-aft and height window.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect slider travel after frontal contact. Test roller grip and range separation with folded flanges, soft cubes and parts shifted by impact.
subsystems.unknowns: Roller materials, exact reductions and capture probability by approach angle.

subsystems.name: Sensing, cross-slide and transfer
subsystems.construction: Time-of-flight ranging, powered transverse scoring slide, vertical elevator and coordinated transfer commands.
subsystems.operation: Orientation selects the measurement pose. Filtered range plus an offset sets the lateral position. Roller release and receiving commands overlap as the system clears the exchange.
subsystems.team_rationale: The lateral slider was added because the piece can land anywhere across the roller span. The team wanted handoff across that span.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A clamped axis target can still be unreachable for the jaw. Test the edges for transfer completion, not just encoder arrival.
subsystems.interfaces: Sensor line of sight couples piece geometry to axis position. The gripper, elevator, arm and intake are all command requirements during handoff.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: After replacing sensors or guides, verify tip-in/out readings and transverse offset. Try an interrupted exchange with a half-seated piece.
subsystems.unknowns: Drop detection and recovery rates, precise sensor mounting and calibration tolerances.

subsystems.name: Scoring linkage and operator interface
subsystems.construction: Non-parallel four-bar with an Everybot-style roller gripper on the elevating assembly. The original driver-station keyboard selected scoring location.
subsystems.operation: The linkage extends to the mid and high rows. The driver later aligned manually while the operator selected piece type and row.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team chose the linkage for reach and lower weight. It reports the driver eventually outperformed the automatic location-scoring sequence.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Evaluate both manual and automatic release against total time and repeatability once the drive team has practiced. Tip grip makes cone attitude sensitive to contact slip.
subsystems.interfaces: Four-bar, elevator and transverse slide stack loads between the claw and chassis.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check joint play at extended poses and verify that a slipped cone still clears the node during retract.
subsystems.unknowns: Arm transmission, grid clearance under load and measured manual-versus-automatic performance.

revisions: The team chose the pasta roller after testing other roller intakes. The driver-operator split shifted from target selection plus automatic scoring to manual alignment with operator piece and level selection.
transferable_principles: Reduce many initial piece orientations to a few stable sensed states. Use independent axes for independent handoff errors when the cycle savings justify the control work.
disconfirming_conditions: The strategy weakens if single-substation feed is inconsistent, range estimates overlap for malformed pieces or alignment and retries consume the saved travel time.
remaining_gaps: Matched cycle-time trials, deployment chronology, full transmission specifications and end-to-end acquisition and recovery measurements.
